summary.motive: Get the ball to the perimeter instantly, before any rush or coverage reaction can develop, and let a two-man convoy block the only defenders who trigger correctly.
summary.whyItWorks: The ball leaves at 0.6 seconds — faster than any pressure plan — and the guards’ two-count pass-set sell buys clean release paths; the TE and H form the convoy while the MIKE’s correct trigger still forces him into a losing lateral chase through traffic.
summary.failureMode: A RCB who beats the H arc to the catch point and a NICKEL who slips the TE log quickly — if the first two defenders to arrive make immediate tackles, the screen becomes a wasted down.

beats.title: 1. The Pre-Loaded Throw
beats.text: This is a called shot, not a read: the QB takes a half hitch and delivers by 0.6 seconds. Every defensive reaction after that is happening to a ball that is already gone.

beats.title: 2. OL Sells Set, Then Releases
beats.text: The guards sold two counts of drop-back protection, freezing the interior rush — then both slip out. The 3T is still fighting a punch that no longer exists while his target runs the other way.

beats.title: 3. Convoy Forms
beats.text: TE logs the apex NICKEL at the line and H cracks the RCB in the alley, building a moving wall before Z even reaches full speed. Two blockers for every defender who triggered properly.

beats.title: 4. MIKE Chases Laterally
beats.text: The MIKE triggers correctly but must run sideways through traffic while the released guards climb to the second level. This lateral chase against a moving convoy is exactly the geometry Payton wants.

beats.title: 5. Turn the Corner
beats.text: With the SS forced into an over-the-top run-down and the FS taking a hopeless angle from middle field, Z presses the numbers behind the RT escort. Six blockers, eleven yards of green.

relations.tell: The ball is out at ~0.6s with zero route development, and the TE plus slot sprint into blocking arcs instead of routes — pure convoy geometry.
